title: Commit message habits to stop (from the 2026-11-26 review)
description:
A review of 25 commit messages written on 2026-11-26 found three habits.
They are already pushed, so this is about not repeating them. Candidate
rules for AGENTS.md's Commits section, held because AGENTS.md is Mark's
file and was itself under review.

## 1. Never write the history of the patch

No "an earlier version", "I built X before Y", "my first argument
claimed", "which was the option I recommended", "I had argued that". A
rejected alternative is recorded as a property of the design -- "not
MAX(room_event.fanout_seq), because retention deletes event rows" --
never as a story about the author. Test: if a sentence has an author in
it, delete the author and see whether anything is left.

One message contained "and his instinct found it", which is flattery in
a permanent record.

## 2. Stop at the last fact

No closing aphorism, moral or announced lesson: "it can promise the loss
is never silent", "an argument is not a test", "named because they are
losses and not cleanups". The restatement always hides in the final
paragraph, which is why reading a message bottom-up finds it.

## 3. No preambles, no CAPS, no gate reports

Never announce a list ("Three choices the design note did not force",
"Two things follow, and both are why this beats X"). Never emphasise
with capitals (NOT, SAME, CANNOT, TWO appeared across four messages);
rewrite the sentence. Never "it is not only X"; give X's reason. Test
counts and gate results: one line at most, never an argument from them,
since "2181 tests pass" is true of every commit and dates instantly.
Subject lines stay at 72 characters; four exceeded it, one at 79.

## The structural finding, which is worth more than the style

Two messages written as advocacy did not survive the morning.
8621e9cb argued for participantIds, including "Mark accepted that";
b195ea2d reverted it an hour later. ebb833d1 argued why its table "beats
mapping the membership changes"; 5200b1dd deleted that table five
commits on. A message that argues why an approach WINS, rather than
stating what it does and what it costs, is the one that reads worst
after a revert.

Same class: 670dd315 asserts "the hub answers 410", which de9a99c0
changed hours later. A commit message that describes the wire format in
passing dates fast.

The best message of the day was 0422558e, which gave numbers that earned
their place and a paragraph on what the change gives up.
